news_title: Thousands of Mercedes-Benz and Fuso trucks recalled in SA - TimesLIVE
efet_title: Thousands of Mercedes-Benz and Fuso trucks recalled in SA - TimesLIVE
efet_body:
The National Consumer Commission (NCC) has notified consumers of safety and compliance recalls affecting thousands of Mercedes-Benz and Fuso trucks and buses sold in South Africa.
The recalls were notified to the NCC by Daimler Truck Southern Africa (DTSA), which said some of the affected vehicles have already been repaired.
The largest outstanding recall involves Mercedes-Benz Actros 963 and Arocs 964 trucks, where a defective axle bearing bracket could loosen, potentially causing the rear axle to become misaligned and affecting the vehicle’s driving and braking characteristics.
The axle bearing bracket guides the rear axle longitudinally and the supplier has identified cases where it can loosen, typically after about 600,000km. If screws or nuts are lost, the resulting axle misalignment could increase the risk of an accident.
The affected trucks were made available for sale from 2022 onwards. A total of 1,538 trucks remain outstanding for repair.
A further 966 Fuso FJ trucks remain to be repaired after the supplier identified a risk of cracking in high-pressure fuel pipes. Excessive stress caused by vibration and surface abnormalities can cause the pipes to crack around bends and, in the worst case, result in fuel leakage.
The recall affects Fuso FJ trucks made available for sale from 2022 onwards.
Another 815 Fuso Fighter FK, FM and FN trucks, sold from 2017 onwards, are affected by oxidation on an electrical contact surface. This can cause the turn indicators to fail intermittently, while the corresponding flasher indication on the instrument cluster may also fail.
The Fuso Canter FE8 7-150 and FE 8-150 are subject to a software-related recall affecting the instrument cluster LCD. The display can black out or fade when the ignition is switched on and off within a short period, while high cabin temperatures of about 60°C can also cause the display to fade. A total of 124 trucks remain to be repaired.
Mercedes-Benz Arocs 964 trucks made available from 2022 onwards are also affected by a potentially serious front-axle issue. Screws securing the front axle leaf-spring assembly may become loose, allowing the axle to move during braking.
This could cause the truck to pull strongly to one side, making it difficult for the driver to maintain the vehicle’s lane and increasing the risk of an accident. Sixty-two trucks remain outstanding for repair.
A separate recall affecting Mercedes-Benz Actros 963, Arocs 964, Atego 967 and electric eActros 983 trucks concerns incorrectly soldered components on the accelerator pedal’s printed circuit board.
If a voltage peak occurs, the accelerator pedal sensor could fail, resulting in a loss of throttle response. The truck could then coast to a halt and become immobile, potentially creating a hazard in traffic. The braking, lighting and warning-lamp functions remain available.
Seven trucks remain to be repaired.
Eight Mercedes-Benz model 2445 buses, sold from 2025 onwards, have also yet to be presented for inspection and remediation. Their engines may have missing or incorrect parameters and wiring configurations that could affect the aftertreatment system and result in the buses not fully complying with applicable particulate and NOx emission requirements.
The NCC said owners of affected vehicles should take them to their nearest authorised Daimler Truck dealer for inspection and the necessary repairs.
All corrective work will be carried out at no cost to consumers, the commission said.
Queries relating to the recalls can be directed to
ProductRecall@thencc.org.za
.

The National Consumer Commission has warned consumers about a recall of certain shampoo products from Woolworths.
The retailer said a limited batch of the 250ml w.beauty complete clarifying shampoo has tested positive for a rod-shaped bacterium known to contaminate water-based cosmetic products.

Ford Ranger recall in SA: Is your bakkie on the list?
Ford Ranger recall in SA: Is your bakkie on the list?
This batch of Ford Rangers are being recalled in South Africa and neighbouring countries. Here’s what you need to know…
By
Alicia Naidoo
Published Aug 31, 2026
Updated Aug 31, 2026
in
News
0
Ford Ranger recalled in SA. Image: Pexels
If you’re one of the thousands of proud
Ford Ranger
owners in South Africa, it might be worth checking your VIN this week.
The
National Consumer Commission (NCC)
has announced a new safety recall affecting
2 275
Ford Ranger Double Cabs, due to concerns with the side curtain airbags.
WHAT’S THE ISSUE?
According to National Consumer Commission (NCC) spokesperson Phetho Ntaba, the side curtain airbags in the affected vehicles may interact with the B-pillar trim during inflation and fail to deploy as intended.
ADVERTISEMENT
If that happens, the B-pillar ramp could detach from the vehicle entirely and become a projectile inside the cabin when the airbag goes off.
In plain terms: in a crash where the airbag is meant to protect you, a loose piece of trim could become a hazard of its own, increasing the risk of injury to anyone inside.
WHICH VEHICLES ARE AFFECTED?
The recall covers Ford Ranger Double Cab models from the 2026 to 2027 model years, sold nationwide through Ford’s franchised dealerships between 22 May and 23 June 2026.
It’s not just a South African problem, either.
The recall also extends to units exported to Namibia, Botswana, Lesotho and Eswatini, meaning bakkie owners across the region should be paying attention too.
HOW TO CHECK IF YOUR BAKKIE IS ON THE LIST AND WILL IT COST YOU?
Owners are urged to check their Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) against the affected list.
ADVERTISEMENT
This can typically be done via Ford South Africa’s official recall page, or by contacting an authorised Ford dealership directly with your VIN in hand.
If your Ranger is affected, the fix is free.
Ford dealerships will inspect and repair the airbag system at no cost to the owner, so there’s no reason to put off booking that appointment.
NOT THE FIRST RECALL IN 2026
This isn’t the Ranger’s first trip into recall territory in 2026.
Earlier this year, Ford issued a recall for over
5 600
2025 and 2026 model year Rangers across Southern Africa after identifying a fault that could cause a loss of brake boost, making vehicles harder to stop.
Back in April, another batch of Rangers and Pumas were recalled over a faulty EGR valve that could cause a sudden loss of engine power at low speeds.
And in July, the NCC flagged transmission fluid pump gear issues in previous-generation Rangers and Everest SUVs sold between 2018 and 2020.
The Ford Rangers weren’t the only vehicles being recalled.
The NCC has also recently dealt with recalls affecting
Nissan Qashqai
models over a fuel pipe fault.
The NCC says it will continue monitoring this recall, along with others, to ensure all affected vehicles in South Africa are properly attended to.
For Ranger owners, a quick trip to the dealership now could make all the difference later.

Selected Toyota models have been recalled over an instrument-display fault that could prevent drivers from seeing important vehicle warnings. Photo: Stock.
Toyota drivers have been urged to check whether their vehicles are affected by a recall involving 518 cars sold across South Africa.
The recall affects selected Toyota RAV4 PHEV, Corolla Cross, Corolla Hatchback, Crown and GR Corolla vehicles.
The
National Consumer Commission
(NCC) announced the recall after Toyota South Africa Motors notified it.
According to the NCC, the recall relates to a programming problem affecting the combination meter. This system displays warning and indicator lights, gauges and other vehicle messages on the 12.3-inch instrument screen.
The affected vehicles include:
16 RAV4 PHEV vehicles built from July 8, 2024 onwards
Four Corolla Cross vehicles built from July 2, 2024 onwards
391 Corolla Hatchback vehicles built from October 7, 2022 onwards
21 Crown vehicles built from October 17, 2022 onwards
86 GR Corolla vehicles built from February 16, 2023 onwards
Not every vehicle built after these dates is necessarily affected. Owners should contact an authorised Toyota dealership and provide their vehicle identification number, or VIN, to confirm whether their particular car is included.
The NCC said unnecessary data may be repeatedly written to a memory device because the combination meter was improperly programmed.
This could cause the device to deteriorate sooner than intended and may cause the instrument display to fail to show information when the vehicle is started.
Should another vehicle malfunction occur while the display is not working, the driver may not see the relevant warning or indicator light.
A notification may appear on the vehicle’s central multimedia screen. However, motorists who do not notice it could continue driving without realising a vehicle malfunction.
“Depending on the malfunction, continued driving may increase the risk of an accident,” the NCC warned.
Acting NCC commissioner Hardin Ratshisusu urged consumers to take recall notices seriously and ensure affected vehicles are presented to the manufacturer for the necessary work.
The repair involves reprogramming the combination meter assembly and will be carried out free of charge at an authorised Toyota dealership.
Vehicle recalls have increased sharply in South Africa in recent years.
According to NCC figures reported by
Wanted Online
, recall campaigns increased from 25 during the 2023/24 financial year to 35 in 2024/25, before rising to 75 in 2025/26.
Mechanical and physical faults involving engines, transmissions, brakes, steering systems, airbags and fuel systems still account for most recalls. However, an increasing number now involve software, electronic control units and digital displays.
NCC spokesperson Phetho Ntaba told the publication the increase could indicate greater transparency rather than deteriorating vehicle quality, as manufacturers identify defects and notify consumers earlier.
Toyota corporate communications manager Refilwe Ramatlhodi Ndhlovu said recall and service campaigns form an important part of the manufacturer’s commitment to quality, durability and reliability.
Modern vehicles contain numerous electronic control units and millions of lines of software code, meaning faults can sometimes affect every vehicle using the same programming.
Owners of the affected Toyota models should contact their nearest authorised dealership with their 17-character VIN and arrange the free repair if required.
The VIN can ordinarily be found on the vehicle’s licence disc, registration documents or identification plate.
Toyota South Africa’s customer contact centre can be reached on
0800 139 111
. Recall-related enquiries may also be sent to the NCC at
ProductRecall@thencc.org.za
.
